header.contentDescription: How a four-stroke engine works: an animated cylinder cross-section with four steps, intake, compression, power and exhaust, and previous, next and play controls.

EngineScreen.summary: A four-stroke engine walkthrough: cylinder drawing, steps, caption and controls

taps.doc: counts step changes, eased to animate a stroke

semantics.contentDescription: Cross-section of one engine cylinder. The piston slides in the cylinder and is joined by a connecting rod to the crankshaft below. The intake valve is on the left, the exhaust valve on the right and the spark plug at the top. Gas in the cylinder is drawn as filled dots for the fresh fuel and air mixture, star marks for burning gas and rings for exhaust gas, and is labelled beside the cylinder.

text.value: The intake valve opens and the piston moves down, drawing a fresh mixture of fuel and air into the cylinder. The exhaust valve stays closed.
Both valves close. The piston moves back up and squeezes the mixture into the small space under the spark plug, which makes it hot.
The spark plug fires and the mixture burns. The hot gas expands and pushes the piston down, turning the crankshaft: the only stroke that makes power.
The exhaust valve opens and the piston moves up again, pushing the burnt gas out. Then the intake valve opens and the cycle starts over.
